high_level_description: A wordless 1940s French railway safety-poster illustration shows a rural manual-block station after one train has entered a fog-hidden single-track section, while a railway guard listens for the missing arrival notice and keeps a following locomotive behind the closed mechanical semaphore, with flat gouache color and firm lithographic contours.

compositional_deconstruction.background: An isolated single-track station in the French Jura around 1940, with pale rendered walls, dark timber eaves, a narrow platform, telegraph poles and steel rails curving into dense valley fog that completely conceals the railway and downstream post beyond the curve. A thinning remnant of coal smoke hangs there under cool overcast daylight. No writing, numerals, arrows, diagrams, modern screens, colored lamps or symbolic overlays.

elements.desc: French railway block guard seated inside the open office window, middle-aged man with light-brown skin, short black hair, navy wool cap, navy jacket, cream shirt, gray trousers and black boots. He presses a black telephone receiver to one ear, watches the fog-hidden line with a tense attentive expression, and keeps his free hand withdrawn from the block lever.

Wall-mounted railway telephone inside the office, made from dark varnished oak with a black earpiece, separate speaking horn, twin brass bells and a cloth-covered cord reaching the guard’s hand. Its bells remain still and the apparatus carries no readable maker’s plate, message slip, alphabet, number, indicator flag or decorative emblem.

Period French manual-block apparatus beside the guard, comprising a dark cast-iron block instrument, brass call bell, hand crank and one tall wooden-handled semaphore lever linked to the trackside signal. The lever remains mechanically caught in its stop position, with no illuminated display, readable plaque, painted status field, loose token, extra control or invented interlock mechanism.

Full-height French mechanical railway semaphore standing beside the single track, with a riveted iron mast, access ladder, counterweight, steel operating cable and one broad vermilion arm edged in white. The arm rests horizontally across the line-of-travel position, physically holding the section closed; the mast has no lamp, arrow, letter, numeral or modern signal head.

Following French steam locomotive, the only visible train, waiting several metres before the semaphore in three-quarter front view, with black boiler, dark green cab, red-brown buffer beam and three coupled driving wheels. Its side rods are still, brakes applied and a small vertical plume escapes the chimney; no driver, crest, number, destination board or company name appears.
